note: Advice library. Only tips with status 'verified' are shown in the app. Statuses are set by scripts/verify_tips.py, which fetches each source and confirms the quote; quotes are recorded only from fetched pages, never from memory. See CLAUDE.md ground rule 1.

tips.text: To decide a call, compare your equity with the price: you need at least call ÷ (pot + bet + call). A half-pot bet needs 25%, a pot-sized bet 33%.

sources.name: Pot odds
sources.quote: pot odds are the ratio of the current size of the pot to the cost of a contemplated call

sources.name: Learn How to Calculate Pot Odds with GTO Wizard
sources.quote: Required Equity to Call = (Call Amount) / (Total Pot After Calling)

checks.detail: call / (pot + bet + call) gives 25% for a half-pot bet, 33.3% for a pot bet, 40% for 2x pot

tips.text: Quick estimate for a draw: multiply your outs by 4 with two cards to come, by 2 with one card to come, and compare that percentage with the price. It's close for ordinary draws and overstates very big ones (15 outs is about 54%, not 60%).

sources.name: Pot odds (rule of 2 and 4 example)
sources.quote: This gives a probability of 9/46 (19.6%). The rule of 2 and 4 estimates Alice's equity at 18%.

sources.name: Rule of 2 and 4 explained
sources.quote: If you are on the turn, multiply your outs by 2. If you are on the flop with the turn and river both still to come, multiply your outs by 4. The number you get is your rough equity as a percent.

checks.detail: 9 outs: exact hit chance 35.0% by the river vs rule 36%; 19.6% on one card vs rule 18%. (Equity vs a random hand is higher: 72% / 35%, since the draw can also win unimproved.)

tips.text: In Omaha, a hand that isn't the nuts is far weaker than it looks against several opponents: small flushes lose value multiway, and even a flopped nut straight with no redraw is often a fold when the money goes in.

sources.name: Eight Common Mistakes Beginners Make in Pot-Limit Omaha
sources.quote: In pot-limit Omaha smaller flushes than queen-high don't have much value when facing multiple opponents. You should be very careful about calling off or value betting your flushes.

sources.name: Pot-Limit Omaha Strategy: When Do You Fold The Nuts?
sources.quote: big mistakes I often see PLO beginners do is to stack off many big blinds in a pot where they flop a straight without redraw versus multiple opponents

tips.notes: Needs a second independent publisher confirmed (two PokerNews pages count once). Candidate sources from a web search on 2026-10-25.

tips.text: In Omaha the nuts on the flop is often only the temporary nuts: with cards to come, a nut hand with no redraw can be overtaken, and strong players sometimes fold it. The nuts plus a draw to a better nuts is a different hand entirely.

sources.name: Introduction to Omaha Poker - The Temporary Nuts
sources.quote: The point I am making is that in Omaha, the Temporary Nuts are dangerous. To be dealt the nut hand at the flop can be an accident waiting to happen if the texture of the flop is such that multiple draws are likely to have hit other players' hands.

sources.name: Pot-Limit Omaha Strategy: When Do You Fold The Nuts?
sources.quote: It is true that sometimes the right play is to throw your hand away, even if you are currently holding the nuts. It is a basic situation where you have flopped the nut straight and you have no redraw with it.

tips.text: Open fewer hands from early position and more from late position: with many players still to act behind you, you'll be raised more often and play most hands out of position after the flop.

sources.name: Early Position in Poker — Definition & Tips
sources.quote: Because early position players act before most of the table, they lack information about how many opponents will enter the pot and how aggressively, which increases the risk of being outplayed postflop. As a result, standard strategy calls for tighter opening ranges from early position compared to later seats like the cutoff or button.

sources.name: Best Poker Opening Ranges by Position You Should Use
sources.quote: That's why you play fewer hands from early position and open much wider near the button.

sources.name: 6-max preflop charts: free GTO ranges for every position
sources.quote: The ranges widen seat by seat, from 17.6 % of hands in the lojack to 43.6 % on the button.

checks.detail: real 6-max charts open UTG 18%, HJ 22%, CO 29%, BTN 44%

tips.notes: Three publishers; Pokalab's figure is solver output (6-max, 100bb, GGPoker NL50 rake). Will also be checked against imported charts (chart_sanity) in phase 7.

tips.text: The shorter your stack, the more hands you should be willing to shove: with few blinds left, the blinds you pick up are worth more relative to what you risk.

sources.name: Push/Fold Strategy
sources.quote: you are risking fewer chips to win the same reward, so the shorter you get, the more hands clear that bar

sources.name: Push-Fold (glossary)
sources.quote: Shoving frequencies climb sharply as the stack gets shorter; from the small blind at five BB you can shove most playable hands without needing post-flop play.

checks.detail: heads-up solver: 130 shoving classes at 5bb vs 91 at 15bb

tips.notes: Needs a second publisher; both quotes are PokerSkill. The program's solver confirms the direction (math check).

tips.text: With antes in play there's more dead money in the pot before anyone acts, so both shoving and calling ranges get wider than without antes.

sources.name: Push/Fold Strategy
sources.quote: Antes push every one of those bars further right, because they add dead money to the reward without changing what you risk.

sources.name: Push or Fold: Master Short-Stack Tournament Poker
sources.quote: Antes expand all pushing ranges by 20 to 30 percent, while ICM pressure (bubble or pay jumps) tightens calling ranges substantially.

sources.name: Short-Stack Tournament Strategy Guide
sources.quote: With antes in play, you are frequently getting 3-to-1 or better to call a shove, which means your calling range widens dramatically

checks.detail: heads-up 10bb: push 113 -> 119 classes, call 69 -> 77 with antes

tips.notes: Two publishers plus the program's solver (math check).

tips.text: Pot-limit sizing: first count the pot as if you had called, then raise by that amount on top. Max raise to = largest bet + (pot including all bets + your call).

sources.name: Raise in Poker (rules glossary)
sources.quote: In pot-limit poker, the maximum raise is limited by the current size of the pot. You can raise any amount up to the pot total after calling the current bet.

sources.name: Pot-Limit Texas Hold'em
sources.quote: If you want to raise, the pot is calculated as though you already had called.

sources.name: Raise (glossary)
sources.quote: In pot limit games, you cannot raise more than the total size of the current pot.

tips.notes: Rule of the game. Dummies' worked example (1/2 blinds, under the gun: raise up to $5 on top of the $2 call, i.e. to $7) matches the program's answer of 7.

tips.text: Suited versions of a hand carry a little more equity than the offsuit version (typically 2-3 points) because of the extra flush chances, so suited hands are generally played from more positions than the same hand offsuit.

sources.name: Offsuit (glossary)
sources.quote: The difference in equity between suited and offsuit versions of the same hand is typically around 2-3%, which is meaningful but usually not decisive on its own for preflop decisions.

sources.name: Offsuit in Poker: Meaning, Notation, and Offsuit vs Suited
sources.quote: The suited version, AKs, is usually stronger because both cards share a suit and can make a flush together.

checks.detail: equity table: suited beats the same hand offsuit vs 22 by 2.6%, 2.3%, 4.5%

tips.notes: The equity table confirms the size of the edge (2.6% AKs/AKo, 2.3% T9s/T9o, 4.5% 72s/72o vs 22).
